title: Justify-content and align-items
learningObjectives: Explain justify-content and align-items and build a practical layout with it.

understand.concept: justify-content aligns flex items along the main axis, while align-items aligns them along the cross axis for each flex line. Values include start, end, center, space-between, and stretch where applicable. The result depends on flex-direction and available space.
understand.whyItMatters: These properties are axis-relative. If flex-direction changes from row to column, the meaning of main-axis and cross-axis alignment changes too.
understand.analogy: One control arranges items along the line; the other aligns them across the line.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual flex layout follows the flex formatting algorithm and writing-mode rules.

explain.narrative: The items spread along the main axis and align centrally on the cross axis.

examples.explanation: The items spread along the main axis and align centrally on the cross axis.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered demonstration of the layout concept.

practise.guidedTask: Try center, space-between, and flex-end for justify-content. Change align-items and then switch flex-direction to column.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive component using this concept. Test long labels, narrow widths, and keyboard navigation.
hints: Inspect the flex container and items in developer tools.
Change one axis or alignment property at a time.
Test with translated or longer labels.
